content:
1. Acceptance of Terms

By registering, accessing or using the HealthHome application, the user agrees to these Terms & Conditions and the applicable Privacy Policy, Refund & Cancellation Policy and service-specific policies.

The user must provide accurate information and use the application lawfully.

If the user creates or manages a family member's profile, they confirm that they are authorised to provide their information and manage their account.

2. About HealthHome

HealthHome provides a digital platform to help users discover and access participating doctors, pharmacies and laboratories.

HealthHome facilitates digital connections, appointment requests, orders, payments and service-related communication.

Healthcare services are provided by independent doctors, pharmacies and laboratories.

Unless expressly stated otherwise, HealthHome does not itself diagnose medical conditions, prescribe medicines, manufacture or dispense medicines, collect or analyse laboratory samples, or issue medical reports.

3. Doctor Consultations

- Users are responsible for providing accurate medical history, symptoms, current medicines, allergies and other relevant information.
- A doctor may request additional information or decline a consultation if clinically inappropriate.
- Video or online consultation may not be suitable for every medical condition.
- The doctor is responsible for clinical assessment, diagnosis, advice, prescriptions and professional decisions.
- The application must not be used as a substitute for emergency medical services.
- Users may be asked to provide consent before teleconsultation.

4. Medicines and Pharmacy Orders

- Medicine orders are fulfilled by participating pharmacies, subject to availability and applicable prescription requirements.
- Users must upload a genuine and valid prescription wherever required by law.
- Pharmacists may review prescriptions and request clarification or confirmation of a final bill.
- Unauthorised substitutions are prohibited.
- Users should check medicine name, quantity, packaging, expiry date and bill upon delivery.
- Damaged, tampered or questionable medicines must be reported promptly.

5. Laboratory Services

- Laboratory tests and sample collection are provided by participating laboratories and their authorised personnel.
- Users must provide accurate patient details and follow preparation instructions.
- Collection and availability depend on location and service area.
- Laboratories are responsible for sample handling, testing, quality procedures and reports.
- Report-related questions should be directed to the laboratory or a qualified healthcare professional.

6. Family Profiles and Account Security

Users are responsible for protecting their login credentials.

For family profiles:

- Provide accurate information.
- Obtain permission before managing another adult's health information.
- Use a child's profile only as a parent or legally authorised guardian.
- Do not access another person's health information without authority.

7. Payments, Bills and Refunds

Payments may be processed through authorised payment service providers.

HealthHome may facilitate payment collection and settlement to participating providers according to the applicable payment arrangement.

Users must review displayed prices and charges before confirmation.

Refunds, cancellations, rescheduling and failed transactions are governed by the Refund & Cancellation Policy and applicable law.

Where a provider fails to deliver a confirmed service, HealthHome will coordinate an appropriate resolution.

Unlawful cancellation charges must not be imposed.

8. User Responsibilities and Prohibited Conduct

Users must not:

- Provide false identity, prescription, payment or medical information.
- Misuse another person's account.
- Harass or abuse healthcare providers or support personnel.
- Upload unlawful or misleading content.
- Disrupt or misuse the application.
- Use HealthHome for unlawful activities.

9. Privacy and Health Information

HealthHome and participating providers may process relevant information to provide requested services, subject to the Privacy Policy and applicable law.

Users should only upload information they are authorised to share.

10. Provider Responsibility and HealthHome's Role

Doctors are responsible for professional medical services.

Pharmacies are responsible for lawful dispensing and fulfilment.

Laboratories are responsible for sample collection, testing and reports.

HealthHome remains responsible for its own platform operations, representations, payment obligations, data handling and statutory duties.

11. Complaints and Grievances

Users may submit complaints through in-app support or the official support email.

Complaints must be handled according to applicable law.

12. Suspension or Termination

HealthHome may restrict or suspend accounts for fraud, unlawful activity, abuse, security risks or serious breaches.

Where reasonably possible, users will be informed of the reason and available resolution process.

13. Changes to These Terms

Material changes will be communicated through the application or another appropriate method.

Continued use will be subject to applicable law and required consent.

14. Governing Law

These terms are governed by Indian law and applicable courts or forums.

Acceptance confirms that the user has read and understood these terms.
title: HealthHome – Patient / Individual User Terms & Conditions

content:
1. Acceptance and Eligibility

Doctors confirm that they hold valid recognised medical qualifications and current professional registration with the appropriate State Medical Council or National Medical Commission register, as applicable.

All submitted qualifications, registration details and identity information must be genuine and accurate.

Doctors must promptly notify HealthHome of any change in their right to practise.

2. Independent Professional Status

Doctors are independent medical professionals using HealthHome as a technology platform.

They are not employees, agents or representatives of HealthHome merely because they use the platform.

Doctors retain independent clinical judgment.

3. Credential Verification

Doctors authorise HealthHome to verify identity, qualifications, registration, contact details and credentials.

Doctors must not use the Doctor Workspace until approval is granted.

HealthHome may suspend access for false, expired or unverifiable credentials.

4. Professional and Clinical Responsibilities

Doctors must:

- Follow applicable laws, ethics and professional standards.
- Follow applicable Telemedicine Practice Guidelines.
- Obtain patient consent before teleconsultation.
- Assess whether online consultation is appropriate.
- Recommend in-person or emergency care when required.
- Maintain appropriate clinical notes and prescriptions.
- Protect patient confidentiality.
- Prescribe within professional competence.
- Avoid misleading claims, unnecessary tests and unethical conduct.

Doctors remain responsible for clinical assessments, diagnoses, advice and prescriptions.

5. Appointments and Attendance

Doctors must:

- Maintain accurate availability.
- Respond promptly to appointments.
- Join confirmed consultations on time.
- Notify patients and HealthHome of attendance issues.
- Avoid accepting appointments they cannot fulfil.

Repeated unexplained cancellations may result in warnings or suspension.

6. Patient Communication

Doctors must communicate professionally and respectfully.

They must not harass, discriminate against, threaten or exploit patients.

Patient contact details must not be misused for unauthorised marketing or solicitation.

7. Fees, Payments and Settlements

Consultation fees and platform charges must be disclosed or agreed before offering services.

HealthHome may facilitate payment collection and settlement to verified accounts.

Doctors must provide accurate bank and tax details and complete required KYC.

Platform fees must be documented in a separate commercial schedule and comply with applicable professional rules.

Nothing authorises unlawful referral commissions or fee-sharing.

8. Cancellations, No-Shows and Refunds

Doctors must notify HealthHome promptly if unable to attend.

HealthHome may coordinate rescheduling or refunds when a confirmed consultation is not provided.

Financial recovery must be disclosed, evidence-based and legally permissible.

9. Patient Data and Confidentiality

Doctors must:

- Access only necessary patient information.
- Maintain confidentiality.
- Use secure devices.
- Avoid unauthorised copying or disclosure.
- Notify HealthHome of suspected data breaches.
- Follow applicable privacy and medical-record requirements.

10. Prohibited Conduct

Doctors must not submit false credentials, permit unauthorised consultations, issue prescriptions without appropriate assessment, manipulate records or misuse patient information.

11. Suspension and Termination

HealthHome may suspend accounts for credential issues, patient-safety concerns, misconduct, repeated service failures, fraud or data misuse.

12. Liability and Indemnity

Doctors are responsible for their professional acts, omissions and compliance.

Indemnity applies only to the extent permitted by law and does not exclude HealthHome's own statutory or legal responsibilities.

Doctors are encouraged to maintain appropriate professional indemnity insurance.

13. Complaints and Cooperation

Doctors must cooperate with reasonable investigations into complaints and patient-safety issues.

14. Changes and Governing Law

These terms are governed by Indian law and competent courts or forums.

Acceptance confirms the genuineness of credentials and commitment to applicable professional standards.
title: HealthHome – Doctor Partner Terms & Conditions

content:
1. Acceptance and Eligibility

Laboratories confirm that they hold all registrations, licences and approvals required for listed services.

They must maintain suitable premises, testing facilities and qualified personnel.

All submitted documents must be genuine and current.

2. Independent Partner Status

Laboratories operate as independent service providers.

They are responsible for premises, personnel, equipment, sample handling, testing, quality control and reports.

3. Service Listings and Pricing

Laboratories must provide accurate:

- Test and package details.
- Prices and additional charges.
- Home collection availability.
- Preparation instructions.
- Expected report timelines.
- Service limitations.

Undisclosed charges are prohibited.

4. Booking Acceptance and Scheduling

Laboratories must promptly review bookings.

After acceptance they must confirm collection time, assign authorised personnel, communicate delays and avoid false completion updates.

5. Sample Collection and Transport

Laboratories must ensure:

- Appropriate patient identity checks.
- Qualified or authorised collectors.
- Required consent.
- Correct collection materials.
- Accurate labelling.
- Proper storage, packaging and transport.
- Appropriate sample integrity and chain-of-custody procedures.
- Documentation of compromised or rejected samples.

6. Testing and Reports

Laboratories are responsible for testing methods, quality control, accuracy, report authorisation and correct patient identification.

Corrected, amended or withdrawn reports must be communicated appropriately.

Critical results must be communicated according to applicable requirements and clinical protocols.

Reports must never be fabricated or improperly altered.

7. Patient Safety and Communication

Laboratories must treat patients respectfully and provide clear instructions.

Personnel must not provide diagnoses or treatment advice beyond their qualifications and legal authority.

8. Fees, Payments and Settlements

HealthHome may facilitate collection and settlement through authorised payment providers.

Commercial fees, charges, settlement cycle, taxes, refunds and reconciliation must be documented separately.

9. Cancellations, Delays and Refunds

Laboratories must promptly notify HealthHome when services cannot be provided.

They must cooperate in rescheduling, refunds and complaint resolution.

Repeated unjustified failures may result in warnings or suspension.

10. Patient Data and Confidentiality

Laboratories must restrict access to authorised personnel, maintain confidentiality, use appropriate security and report suspected data breaches.

11. Personnel and Compliance

Laboratories are responsible for their employees, contractors, collectors, training and regulatory compliance.

12. Suspension and Termination

HealthHome may suspend laboratories for licence issues, patient-safety concerns, service failures, report manipulation, fraud or data misuse.

13. Liability and Indemnity

Laboratories are responsible for their testing services, collection, reports, personnel and compliance.

Indemnity applies to the extent permitted by law and does not exclude HealthHome's own statutory duties.

14. Complaints and Cooperation

Laboratories must cooperate with complaints, report corrections and sample investigations.

15. Governing Law

These terms are governed by Indian law and competent courts or forums.

Acceptance confirms legal authority to provide listed services.
title: HealthHome – Laboratory Partner Terms & Conditions

content:
1. Acceptance and Eligibility

Pharmacies confirm that they hold valid drug sale licences, required permissions and appropriately qualified pharmacists where required.

Their premises and operations must comply with applicable laws.

All supplied licence and business information must be genuine and current.

2. Independent Partner Status

Pharmacies operate as independent businesses.

They remain responsible for licences, pharmacists, medicine inventory, prescription review, pricing, billing, packaging, dispatch and delivery personnel.

3. Product Listings and Pricing

Pharmacies must ensure:

- Accurate medicine names, strengths, dosage forms and pack sizes.
- Genuine and lawfully sourced products.
- Proper storage conditions.
- No expired, damaged, recalled or counterfeit medicines.
- Accurate prices and charges.
- Updated stock availability.

4. Prescription Review and Pharmacist Responsibilities

Where required by law, pharmacies must obtain and review valid prescriptions.

Qualified pharmacists must perform required professional checks.

Prescription-only medicines must not be supplied without legally required prescriptions.

5. Order Acceptance and Final Bill

The pharmacy must review the order and prescription.

Where necessary, the pharmacist adds appropriate items and sends the final bill.

The patient must confirm material order or price changes before fulfilment.

Unauthorised substitutions are prohibited.

6. Packing and Dispatch

Pharmacies must correctly check medicines, issue invoices, package medicines safely and maintain appropriate storage conditions.

Orders must not be marked dispatched before actual handover.

7. Pharmacy Delivery Personnel

Pharmacies are responsible for selecting and supervising delivery personnel.

Delivery personnel must handle medicines safely, respect patients and protect privacy.

8. Delivery Confirmation and OTP

Where a delivery OTP is used:

- Correct package must be handed to the intended recipient or authorised person.
- Delivery photographs must avoid unnecessary capture of patients or private surroundings.
- OTPs must be handled securely and used only for the relevant order.
- Orders must not be falsely marked delivered.

9. Fees, Payments and Settlements

HealthHome may facilitate collection and settlement through authorised payment providers.

Platform fees, provider charges, settlement, tax treatment and refunds must be documented separately.

Undisclosed charges are prohibited.

10. Cancellations, Unavailable Medicines and Refunds

Pharmacies must promptly report unavailable medicines and delivery failures.

They must cooperate in refunds, replacements and complaint resolution.

11. Patient Data and Confidentiality

Patient information must only be used for lawful prescription review, fulfilment, delivery, billing and record-keeping.

Pharmacies must restrict access, maintain confidentiality and report suspected data breaches.

12. Prohibited Conduct

Pharmacies must not sell counterfeit, expired or unlawfully sourced medicines, supply prescription-only medicines without required prescriptions, falsify records, make unauthorised substitutions or misuse patient data.

13. Suspension and Termination

HealthHome may suspend pharmacies for licence concerns, unlawful medicine supply, safety issues, fraud, repeated failures or data misuse.

14. Liability and Indemnity

Pharmacies are responsible for medicine stock, dispensing, pharmacist review, billing, packaging, delivery and regulatory compliance.

Indemnity applies to the extent permitted by law and does not exclude HealthHome's own legal responsibilities.

15. Complaints and Cooperation

Pharmacies must cooperate with complaints, quality concerns, delivery investigations and refund requests.

16. Governing Law

These terms are governed by Indian law and competent courts or forums.

Acceptance confirms legal authority to operate and fulfil orders.
